x: Of our lads at this time the two Freds—Bentley and Rickards—were together in tenth position, Martin fourteenth, and Paul Khlopin well up. Approaching Croydon, Whitlock drew level with Stone, and shortly afterwards went ahead.
The next two, Bentley and Bidgood, seemed a little lazy, which means they are saving themselves for future events; and sixth came Bob Readman, who continues to improve and promises to do well.
We have held the team title for the last two years; and with Green, Rickards and Bentley, all Olympic possibilities, supported by others, we should claim a "hat trick."

Under this heading in our last issue we expressed our indignation that Bentley had not been invited to accompany the Olympic team to Berlin, and said that it was our intention to take the matter further.

Bentley, with three toenails missing, was an enforced absentee, as were also Green and Rickards. In fact, six only of our men entered, and we must look to it that next year's race will find more of our walkers with the inclination to essay the Brighton course.
Charlie Churcher, Jack Bidgood and Fred Bentley set the pace early on. Pope, Fletcher and Wright preferred to start comparatively slowly, and speed up as the race progressed.
We had hopes of regaining the Championship, but last-minute disappointments robbed us of our chances. It had been intended that Bidgood, Bentley, C.

At 18¾ miles M.W.C. led us 16—22; the Whitlock brothers being 1st and 3rd, their third man, Redman, having dropped to 10th. Fred Bentley was 6th. Fred Rickards was having a bad time, and had dropped back a little.
Bentley and Rickards were among those who retired, but we are always assured of a first-rate performance from these two loyal team men when the National Championship comes along.
Bentley, Sutton, Bidgood and Rickards, At distance-walking, you know they are wizards.
Fred Bentley has been invalided out of the Police after his accident in a plane. He has now started business at the Post Office, Blackmore, Liss, Hants.

George Bentley was second in the handicap and the B Team second in the Team Handicap. A fortnight later in the Enfield Open, the local lads took advantage of their knowledge of the course and narrowly won from us by 3 points.
Team Championship.—3rd Cadogan A.C., 45 points. Readman, 5; Rutland, 10; Oliver, 14; Bentley, 16.

At seven miles Proctor was well away in the lead, Charlie and Mac still 5th and 6th, Readman 12th, Oliver 18th, Sapcote 20th, Bidgood 24th, Bentley 26th, Wright 28th, with Clayton taking it easy owing to a strained leg.

… Pat Sapcote, with Bob McMullen, walking his first 20, some 40 yards further back, followed by Messrs. Wright, Bidgood, Bentley and Oliver. It is interesting to note that Jack Rutland, who finished 4th, was at this stage 12th.…
Much could be written of Tommy Green’s magnificent performances and those of Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and others, but space does not permit.

We have had a number of placed men - Tommy Green on three occasions - but never a winner. Here's a target for next year; to beat our 1938 winning team score of 23 points (Bentley 2, Sutton 4, Bidgood 8 Rickards 9)!
